title: Vergence-accommodation conflict in fixed-focus VR
bottleneck: Every first-generation VR headset is a fixed-focus display: the screen sits at one optical distance while virtual objects demand the eyes converge at many depths. This vergence-accommodation conflict decouples two reflexes that are neurologically linked, causing eyestrain, headaches, and visual fatigue, and it is a leading contributor to VR sickness. Children are advised to avoid such displays entirely due to potential lasting effects.
why_it_blocks: The conflict makes long VR sessions physiologically punishing, blocking VR's use for work, education, and training where hours of wear are required. Until displays focus naturally, VR remains a short-session medium.
current_state: Varifocal prototypes (Meta Half Dome, Lemnis Verifocal) demonstrated relief by moving focal planes with gaze, but no shipping consumer product uses true varifocal optics; multifocal and light-field approaches remain experimental.
